correctness.rationale: Writing omitted vertices as index sets \(I,J\), every omitted vertex needs both a selected and an omitted neighbor across the bipartition. For interior sizes \(2\le|I|,|J|\le n-2\) this is automatic; when either size is one or \(n-1\), exactly the stated matched-index obstruction remains. The case split counts each profile and yields the displayed bivariate polynomial; maximizing \(|I|+|J|\) forces the \((n-1,n-1)\) case with the same omitted index, so the complements are exactly the deleted-matching pairs. I independently replayed the definition for every subset for \(3\le n\le6\), reproducing the minimum sets, while the inspected verifier exhausts all subsets through \(n=9\).

final_claim: For every crown graph \(\operatorname{Cr}_n=K_{n,n}-M\), \(n\ge3\), restrained dominating sets are exactly the four-boundary-condition omission profiles stated in RESULT.md; the resulting bivariate complement enumerator is \(Q_n\), and \(\gamma_r(\operatorname{Cr}_n)=2\) with precisely the \(n\) deleted-matching pairs as minimum sets.
